sql:
SELECT m.month_label,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tickets t WHERE t.created_at >= m.month_start AND t.created_at < m.month_end) AS ticket_count,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM page_views pv WHERE pv.viewed_at >= m.month_start AND pv.viewed_at < m.month_end AND (pv.path ILIKE '%/help%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/kb%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%knowledge%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/faq%' OR pv.path ILIKE '%/support%')) AS kb_engagement_count,
       'page_views.path ILIKE any of %/help%, %/kb%, %knowledge%, %/faq%, %/support% (best-guess pattern)' AS kb_engagement_signal_used
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT month_label, month_start, (month_start + INTERVAL '1 month') AS month_end
  FROM calendar_days
  WHERE calendar_date >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND calendar_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
) m
ORDER BY m.month_label ASC
note: My tooling only lets me validate SQL against an empty schema (dry_run never returns real rows/values), so I could not actually inspect which event_name or path values exist in this warehouse before writing the query. I picked page_views.path with a broad set of help/kb/faq/support/knowledge substring patterns as the most plausible, commonly-used signal, aggregated per calendar month via calendar_days; if these patterns don't match real data, kb_engagement_count will read as 0 rather than NULL, so please sanity-check the first few months before circulating and let me know if the events table turns out to have a better-named view event instead.
